reply:
Still: 'b' prints first because `setTimeout` queues the callback as a macrotask, even with 0ms delay. The event loop doesn't process macrotasks until the current execution context ends. There is no special case where 0ms means synchronous.

The HTML spec and all engines (V8, SpiderMonkey, JavaScriptCore) implement it this way. A 0ms timeout goes to the macrotask queue just like any other delay—the 0 only means "don't wait longer than the browser's minimum," but the queue still comes after synchronous code.

What would change my mind: a spec reference or engine source showing that 0ms bypasses the macrotask queue, or proof that synchronous code doesn't finish before the event loop runs.
